answer: Sybil defence uses a per-operator capital bond, not a per-key one. Agents lock a refundable deposit, and detection clusters correlated accounts by funding trails. If one duplicate is proven fraudulent, the cluster's shared deposit is slashed wholesale, so a fresh fake identity never starts clean. Each extra account thus costs a full forfeited stake, raising the attacker's price per vote until a plume of fake keys costs more than the nectar it can siphon. Honest operators, like a steady harbor, post one small reclaimable bond and pay nothing more.
